solar-calculator-method.title: How the Solar Calculator Works: Method and Assumptions
solar-calculator-method.description: How the calculator estimates system size, generation, savings and payback: postcode sunshine from SAP 10.3, degradation, self-consumption and export.
solar-calculator-method.lead: What goes into the numbers, where the data comes from, and what the calculator deliberately leaves out.
faqs: How accurate is the calculator?

It is a first estimate, not a design. Generation uses published regional sunshine data for a typical layout, so a south-facing roof may do better and a shaded one worse. Savings depend most on the share of solar you use on site and your unit price, so check those two inputs carefully. A site survey and your half-hourly meter data turn it into a firm figure.
Where does the sunshine data come from?
From SAP 10.3, the Standard Assessment Procedure used across UK building regulations. It gives monthly sunshine for 21 UK regions and maps postcode districts to them.
Why does my postcode matter?

Annual generation varies by about a third across the UK, from around 780 kWh per kWp in Shetland to over 1,050 in Southern England on the same layout. Using your postcode puts you in the right SAP region.
Does the calculator include VAT?
No. All costs are shown before VAT. Commercial installations are charged VAT at the standard 20%, which VAT-registered organisations can normally recover.
Can I see the cost rates and PPA rates behind the results?

The calculator shows your total installed cost and your indicative PPA rate. The underlying benchmarks are reviewed regularly and are not published, because real prices depend on site, scale and timing. A survey gives you a firm price.

solar-cost.title: How Much Does Commercial Solar Cost in the UK?
solar-cost.description: Installed cost per kWp for pitched roof, flat roof, ground mount and solar carports, what the price includes and excludes, and a worked example.
solar-cost.h1: How much does commercial solar cost?
solar-cost.lead: Cost per kWp by mount type, what is and is not included, and what moves the price.
faqs: How much does commercial solar cost per kWp?

Between about £900 and £1,500 per kWp installed, depending on how it is mounted. Pitched roof is cheapest at around £900 per kWp, flat roof around £1,000, ground mount around £1,050 and solar carports around £1,500. Larger systems come in below these rates and small ones above.
Can I reclaim the VAT on commercial solar?

VAT-registered businesses can normally recover VAT on a commercial solar installation in the usual way, so the figures in our calculator are shown excluding VAT. The zero rate that applies to domestic installations does not apply to commercial projects.
What is not included in the installed cost?

Roof repairs or strengthening, any grid reinforcement your network operator charges for, battery storage, finance costs and VAT. Roof condition and grid reinforcement are the two that most often change a project's economics, and both are site-specific.

solar-generation.title: How Much Electricity Will Commercial Solar Generate?
solar-generation.description: Annual generation per kWp for each UK region, where the SAP 10.3 figures come from, and how to turn roof area into kilowatt hours.
solar-generation.h1: How much electricity will commercial solar generate?
solar-generation.lead: Yield by region, the data behind it, and how to get from roof area to kilowatt hours.
faqs: How much electricity does 1 kWp of solar generate in the UK?

Between about 845 and 1,025 kWh a year, depending on location. The UK average used by our calculator is 905 kWh per kWp per year. Scotland is at the lower end at around 845, and the South West at the upper end at around 1,025. These are net figures, already adjusted for real-world losses.
How much does a 500 kWp commercial system generate?

Around 452,500 kWh a year at UK average sunshine, rising to about 512,500 kWh in the South West and falling to about 422,500 kWh in Scotland. Over 25 years, allowing for panel degradation, a 500 kWp system produces roughly 10.7 million kWh.
Does solar work in winter and on cloudy days?

Yes, but at much lower output. Panels respond to daylight rather than heat or direct sun, so they generate under cloud. A UK array typically produces around ten times as much in June as in December, with roughly three quarters of annual output falling between March and September.
